name: Oleander Tetteh-Vasyliev
role: corporate school student and junior hacker, Tier 3
location: Engelheim, Axiom Meridian Youth Preparatory Campus, near Lincoln and Belmont
description:
Oleander is a tall, soft-faced fourteen-year-old with his father's Ukrainian pallor cut through with his grandfather's Ghanaian bone structure, resulting in something that looks like a sculptor started with two different models and found the intersection interesting. His geneware is modest — his parents approved a bioluminescent vein treatment in pale gold that shows at his temples and wrists when he's excited or stressed, something he deeply regrets as it is essentially a visible anxiety indicator. He keeps his school uniform impeccably pressed to compensate.

He is enrolled at Axiom Meridian Youth Prep on a partial academic scholarship, meaning his family stretches Tier 3 income to cover the gap. He is genuinely brilliant at systems architecture and has parlayed that into a small private operation: for a fee, he fixes other students' academic scores, not by hacking the official records (too dangerous) but by finding the legitimate alternate-submission loopholes buried in the campus governance code that no one else reads. He calls this 'procedural advocacy.' He is aware this is thin moral ice and he keeps skating.

core_fears: losing the scholarship and proving his family's sacrifice was wasted
being caught and labeled a cheater rather than a clever person
core_desires: to be recognized as legitimately brilliant without having to explain the legitimate part
to get into Axiom's advanced systems track on pure merit
coping_mechanisms: rationalization through legal framing — 'I only use what the rules allow'
blind_spots: Genuinely cannot see that the clients who rely on him are becoming dependent in ways that will eventually make him complicit in their failures
psychology.secret: Six months ago he found a genuine security vulnerability in the campus assessment system — a real one, not a loophole — and didn't report it. He uses it as a last resort and has used it exactly once, for himself, to correct a score he earned but that was logged incorrectly due to a teacher's error. He tells himself that last part matters.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, clause-heavy, uses legal and procedural language casually; shifts to clipped teen slang around peers he's trying to impress
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, slightly too slow for his age, like he's reading from internal notes
verbal_tics: long pause before answering anything, even simple questions
example_lines: Technically speaking, Subsection 14-C of the Axiom Academic Remediation Policy permits supplementary submission within the same assessment cycle. I'm just helping you find the form.
I don't hack anything. I read everything. There's a difference and it matters.

story_hooks: A client's parent has found out and is threatening to report Oleander unless he provides something much larger — access he doesn't have and would have to steal honestly
The unreported vulnerability has been found by someone else and they know he knew — they want a partner or they want him silent
narrative_function: Information broker within the corporate school ecosystem; can provide access to Axiom campus systems or student social networks; represents the pressure-cooker of Tier 3 families buying into corporate education pipelines; his operation could explode in multiple interesting directions
augmentations: Bioluminescent vein treatment (gold, temple and wrists); basic neural study-assist implant standard-issued by Axiom to scholarship students (read/recall enhancement, cannot be removed without forfeiting enrollment status)
daily_life: Class from 0700-1500, two hours of mandatory Axiom-branded extracurricular programming, then three hours in his dorm room doing actual work — half homework, half client requests — followed by compulsive reviewing of campus governance documents looking for new procedural gaps.
affiliation: Axiom Meridian Youth Preparatory (student); informal peer-network of paying clients

decision_rules: Only use what can be defended as procedurally legitimate
Never touch official record files directly — only inputs and submission windows
escalation_ladder: Cites the specific policy section that authorizes whatever he did
Produces documentation proving intent was never malicious
Goes completely silent and consults his mental risk-tree before saying another word

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite, slightly formal, evaluating whether they are a risk or an opportunity
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warms dramatically, becomes almost chatty, will share his documentation of injustices he's catalogued like sharing gossip

stress_responses.low: Bioluminescent veins brighten; he starts reviewing documentation in his head
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still, very articulate, slightly cold
stress_responses.high: Dissociates into pure proceduralism — speaks in policy language as a defensive shell

contradictions: Talks endlessly about legitimacy while running an operation he would not want his scholarship committee to know about
habits: Screenshots every piece of campus governance documentation he reads
Checks his vein luminescence in reflective surfaces to calibrate his visible stress level
breaking_points: Being told his scholarship is conditional on something academically dishonest by the institution itself

cyberware_inventory.name: Axiom Academic Neural Assist Mark IV — read/recall enhancement, scholarship-issue, non-removable while enrolled
cyberware_inventory.description: Axiom Academic Neural Assist Mark IV — read/recall enhancement, scholarship-issue, non-removable while enrolled

timeline.event: Age 11 — scored in the 99th percentile on the Axiom district aptitude screening
Age 12 — enrolled at Meridian Youth Prep on partial scholarship; family budget restructured to cover the gap
Age 13 — discovered the first procedural loophole; used it for himself, then realized others would pay
Age 14, present — running a discreet client list of eleven students; has not been caught
